column2: A village alehouse: a cosy two-storey half-timbered inn with cream plaster and dark oak framing over a stone ground floor, a steep golden straw thatch roof with one eyebrow dormer and a stone chimney, an open arched doorway glowing warm inside, a small timber porch over the door, a carved wooden sign on an iron bracket painted with a frothing tankard, a few oak barrels stacked by the wall, window boxes of red flowers.

A town stable with its paddock: a long low open-fronted timber stable block of dark oak posts and plank stalls under a golden straw thatch roof, four stalls with half-doors along the front, a hayloft door in the gable with hay showing, and in front of the stalls a small square paddock of trodden earth enclosed by a sturdy rustic post-and-rail oak fence on three sides with a wide plank gate in the middle of the far side, a stone water trough and a heap of hay inside the paddock, no horses.

A tall village tower windmill WITHOUT any sails: a tapering round tower of warm grey dressed stone with small arched windows and a plank door at its foot, a wooden cap on top thatched in golden straw, a plain round wooden hub at the front of the cap where the sails will be fixed (no sails, no blades, no arms), a wooden stair to the door, grain sacks by the door.

A village tannery: a timber-framed workshop with plank walls over a stone base and a golden thatch roof, an open-sided lean-to beside it sheltering three round wooden soaking vats of brown water, animal hides stretched on wooden frames drying in front, a rack of hanging leather, a stack of bark in a crate.

A village dyer's workshop: a timber-framed cream plaster house with a red clay-tile roof and stone chimney, an open-sided timber lean-to in front sheltering three big wooden dye vats (one red, one blue, one yellow), long lengths of brightly dyed cloth hanging to dry on poles and lines beside it, a basket of wool.
